title: Basic Geometrical Ideas
description: Class 6 IMO — Basic geometrical ideas: points, lines, line segments and rays, intersecting and parallel lines, types of angles, triangles and the parts of a circle.

topics.title: Points, Lines, Segments & Rays
topics.concept:
A point marks a location. A line extends without end in both directions. A line segment has two endpoints, and a ray has one endpoint and goes on in one direction.

Parallel lines never meet; intersecting lines cross at a point.

examples.problem: How many endpoints does a ray have?
What do we call lines that never meet?

recap: Line: no endpoints; segment: two endpoints; ray: one endpoint.
Parallel lines never meet; intersecting lines cross.

quiz.q: How many endpoints does a line segment have?
quiz.explanation: A line segment has two endpoints.

quiz.q: Two lines that cross at a single point are ___ ?
quiz.explanation: Lines that cross are intersecting lines.

topics.title: Types of Angles
topics.concept:
What are Complementary Angles?

Two angles are complementary if their measures add up to 90°.

  • Each angle is called the complement of the other
  • They don't have to be adjacent (next to each other)

Example: 30° + 60° = 90° → Complementary

What are Supplementary Angles?

Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to 180°.

  • Each angle is called the supplement of the other
  • They don't have to be adjacent

Example: 110° + 70° = 180° → Supplementary

COMPLEMENTARY ANGLES (sum = 90°):

    Adjacent Complementary:     Non-adjacent Complementary:
    
         /|
        / | 30°                    30°
       /  |                          60°
      /   | 60°
     /    |
    └─────┘
    
    30° + 60° = 90°             30° + 60° = 90°


SUPPLEMENTARY ANGLES (sum = 180°):

    Adjacent Supplementary (Linear Pair):   Non-adjacent:
    
        ┌─────────┐
        │         │
        │  120°   │       120°        60°
        │         │
        └─────────┘
    
    120° + 60° = 180°           120° + 60° = 180°


FINDING COMPLEMENTARY ANGLE:

    If one angle is 35°, complement = 90° - 35° = 55°
    If one angle is 72°, complement = 90° - 72° = 18°


FINDING SUPPLEMENTARY ANGLE:

    If one angle is 115°, supplement = 180° - 115° = 65°
    If one angle is 45°, supplement = 180° - 45° = 135°

examples.solution: Between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.

examples.problem: Two angles are complementary. One is 3 times the other. Find both angles.
An angle is 30° more than its supplement. Find the angle.
examples.solution:
• Let angle = x, supplement = 180° - x
  • x = (180° - x) + 30°
  • x = 210° - x
  • 2x = 210°
  • x = 105°
  • Answer: 105°

recap: Angles don't have to be adjacent

quiz.explanation: Between 180° and 360° is a reflex angle.

topics.title: Triangles & Circles
topics.concept: A triangle has 3 sides, 3 vertices and 3 angles. In a circle, the centre is the middle, the radius is the centre-to-edge distance, the diameter goes across through the centre (= 2 × radius), and a chord joins two points on the circle.

examples.problem: A circle has a radius of 5 cm. What is its diameter?
What is the longest chord of a circle called?

recap: Circle: radius = centre to edge; diameter = 2 × radius.

quiz.q: How many vertices does a triangle have?
The fixed distance from the centre to the edge of a circle is the ___ ?

questions.q: Which of these has exactly one endpoint?
questions.explanation: A ray has one endpoint and extends in one direction.

questions.q: A straight angle is to 180° as a right angle is to ___ ?
An angle of 120° is a ___ angle.

questions.explanation: A line segment has two endpoints.

questions.q: A circle has a radius of 7 cm. What is its diameter?
The longest chord of a circle is the ___ ?
questions.explanation: The diameter is the longest chord.

questions.q: Railway tracks are a real-life example of ___ ?
questions.explanation: Railway tracks stay the same distance apart, so they are parallel lines.

questions.q: At 3 o'clock the hands of a clock make a ___ angle.
questions.explanation: At 3:00 the hands are 90° apart — a right angle.

questions.q: How many line segments can be drawn joining two given points?
questions.explanation: Exactly one line segment joins two points.
